title: Flame Photometry Protocol
author: Mariam Awlia
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6t6here

steps.title: Observe safety and PPE
steps.instruction: Work in the fume hood, wear a lab coat, eye protection, gloves, and lower the screen in front of your face; always add acid to water slowly, never water to acid.

steps.title: Prepare 1% nitric acid solution
steps.instruction: For up to 250 samples (250 × 5 = 1.25 L), prepare about 1.5 L of 1 % nitric acid. If using 70 % stock, mix 69 mL Milli‑Q water per 1 mL acid (multiply by 21.4 for 1.5 L). If using 69 % stock, mix 68 mL water per 1 mL acid (multiply by 21.8 for 1.5 L). Example: add 21.8 mL nitric acid to 1483.4 mL Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Weigh and acidify plant samples
steps.instruction: Place each plant sample in a 10 mL Falcon tube, determine its fresh and dry weight, then add 3 mL of the prepared 1 % nitric acid and close the lid tightly.

steps.title: Incubate samples in acid
steps.instruction: After adding acid, let the tubes sit for exactly 03:00:00 (3 h) and shake gently without breaking the rosette to ensure complete coverage.

steps.title: Cool samples before dilution
steps.instruction: Remove the tubes from the acid bath and allow them to cool on the bench before proceeding to dilution.

steps.title: Prepare sample dilutions and standards
steps.instruction: In fresh Milli‑Q water, prepare dilutions with extreme precision and make replicates for each sample. Use two salt and two control Eppendorf tubes to test dilutions and standards before processing the rest. Flip each Falcon tube to remove condensation before pipetting. Suggested dilutions: Salt 1:20 (1.90 mL water + 100 µL sample) and Control 1:5 (1.60 mL water + 400 µL sample). Prepare standards: Salt – 500 µM NaCl and 100 µM KCl; Control – 10–100 µM NaCl and 1000 µM KCl. Avoid carrying any plant fibre into the dilutions.

steps.title: Prepare instrument running and blank solutions
steps.instruction: Fill two beakers with fresh Milli‑Q water: one will serve as the running solution, the other as the blank solution.

steps.title: Initialize flame photometer and computer
steps.instruction: Place the running solution under the U‑tube, add a droplet of water to the connecting tube, open the “air” valve on the main valve and verify liquid draw and waste flow, open the gas bottle fully then turn it back half a turn, switch on the flame photometer and confirm the flame is lit before closing the hatch, turn the computer on for manual recording, and let the running solution flow for 00:30:00 to 01:00:00 before use. Check that the U‑tube contains no air bubbles (wiggle if needed) and that the back‑panel pressure reads approximately 11 psi.

steps.title: Calibrate with blank and standards
steps.instruction: Set the system to dual and peak‑only mode. Insert the blank solution, press “Blank” and wait until the display flashes “100”, then remove the blank. Insert the selected standard solution, press “Cal” for Na and K; when “100” flashes, press “Cal” again. Press “Measure” and wait for the instrument to blink, confirming the blank reads 0 ± 2 and the standard reads 100 ± 2.

steps.title: Measure samples and record values
steps.instruction: Insert each Eppendorf sample, press “Measure”, and wipe the tube with tissue when changing solutions. Record the measured values, applying the expected ranges: Salt 20–120 and Control 10–20.

steps.title: Run periodic standard checks
steps.instruction: After every 12–24 samples, run a standard as a test. When switching between different standard solutions, press “Blank” for 3 seconds to restart calibration.

steps.title: Maintain running solution under U‑tube
steps.instruction: Continuously ensure the running solution remains beneath the U‑tube so the flame photometer does not dry out.

steps.title: Shut down instrument and dispose waste
steps.instruction: Turn the gas valve off and wait until error E61 appears and the flame extinguishes, then switch off the gas and close the air valve. Dispose of all solutions and plant material down the sink with excess water. Verify the waste container is empty and the waste line is flowing properly.
